title: Rejected Verification Documents and the KYC Refresh of an Upgraded Personal Sender Account
content:
Rejected documents, for a Personal Sender Account moved up a level, are the document reviews with the outcome rejected recorded on the account in the 24 months before the upgrade date, a review dated on the same calendar day 24 months earlier or before it no longer counting. When there are 2 or more, 6 months are taken off the risk-weighted refresh interval; when there is exactly 1, 3 months are taken off the risk-weighted refresh interval; when there is none, nothing is taken off for rejected documents.

## Questions this rule answers

**What is counted — documents or reviews?** Reviews. Each review recorded on a document with the outcome rejected counts once, by its review date. Reviews with the outcome accepted do not count.

**Does the rejection reason matter?** No. A rejection as too old, expiring soon, expired, illegible, name mismatch or incomplete counts alike.

**How do the counts map?**

| Rejected reviews in the 24 months before the upgrade date | Months taken off |
|---|---|
| none | 0 |
| exactly 1 | 3 |
| 2 or more | 6 |

**Where does the 24-month window start?** Hypothetical dates: for an upgrade on 8 July, a rejection reviewed on 9 July two years before counts; one reviewed on 8 July two years before, or earlier, no longer counts.
